It goes on 'of the parent or guardian or who has no parent or guardian capable of providing appropriate care.' All parts of the after text match.

title: Grounds for Dependency (WIC Section 300)
statement:
Section 300(g) - No One to Care for the Child
Any one of these: the child was left with no support. Or the child was safely surrendered as a newborn and not taken back in 14 days. Or the parent is in jail or an institution and cannot arrange care. Or the adult caring for the child cannot keep doing it and the parent cannot be found.
source_says: the child has not been reclaimed within the 14-day period ... the child's parent has been incarcerated or institutionalized and cannot arrange for the care of the child
steps: Confirmed live with position() (pos 1329). Opened public.law WIC 300, read subdivision (g) piece by piece: 'left without any provision for support'; surrendered under Health and Safety Code 1255.7 and not reclaimed in 14 days; parent incarcerated or institutionalized; 'a relative or other adult custodian ... is unwilling or unable to provide care or support for the child, the whereabouts of the parent are unknown, and reasonable efforts to locate the parent have been unsuccessful.' All four prongs match. The word 'newborn' is the entry's gloss on section 1255.7; I did not open 1255.7.

title: Timeline for Court Hearings
statement: - If your child was removed, the disposition hearing is usually held within 10 court days after the jurisdiction hearing. Delays should not push it past 60 days after the detention hearing. A judge can go past 60 days only for very unusual reasons, and never past 6 months.
source_says: being completed longer than 60 days, or 30 days in the case of an Indian child, after the hearing at which the minor was ordered removed or detained
steps: Confirmed live with position() (pos 761). Opened public.law 358(a)(1): if the child is detained 'the continuance shall not exceed 10 judicial days' (30 days if the 361.5(b) no-services rule is alleged). Opened public.law 352(b): quoted limit, 'unless the court finds that there are exceptional circumstances', and no continuance past 'six months after the hearing pursuant to Section 319'. The 10 days, 60 days, unusual reasons and 6 months all match. What is left out: for an Indian child the limit is 30 days, not 60.
fix: - If your child was removed, the disposition hearing is usually held within 10 court days after the jurisdiction hearing. Delays should not push it past 60 days after the detention hearing, or 30 days if your child is an Indian child. A judge can go past that only for very unusual reasons, and never past 6 months.

title: Your Rights at the Detention Hearing
statement: 5. Visits: The judge must look at visits at this hearing. The judge decides if contact is good or harmful for your child and then makes visit orders. Ask your lawyer to ask for visits.
source_says: The court must consider the issue of visitation ... determine if contact pending the jurisdiction hearing would be beneficial or detrimental to the child, and make appropriate orders.
steps: Confirmed live with position() (pos 558). Opened rule 5.670 on courts.ca.gov, read the whole Visitation subdivision (c). Entry tracks (c)(1): must consider, decide helpful or harmful, make orders. 'Ask your lawyer to ask for visits' is advice.

title: Your Rights at the Detention Hearing
statement: Cal. Welf. & Inst. Code § 319; Cal. Rules of Court, rules 5.530, 5.534, 5.668, 5.670, 5.674; 25 U.S.C. § 1903(4)
source_says: The following persons are entitled to be present: ... All parents, de facto parents, Indian custodians, and guardians of the child
steps: Confirmed live with position() in legal_reference (pos 1). Opened every cite and matched it to the eight rights. 1 present: rule 5.530(b)(2) (quoted). 2 lawyer and payback: 5.534(c) 'right to have counsel appointed, subject to a claim by the court or the county for reimbursement'. 3 be heard: 5.534(g)(1)(D), WIC 319(a). 4 allegations: 5.668(a). 5 visits: 5.670(c)(1). 6 relatives: WIC 319(h)(2) 'Relatives shall be given preferential consideration'. 7 contest: 319(c)(1), 5.674(c). 8 ICWA: 25 USC 1903(4). One gap: 'Only the tribe decides this' rests on WIC 224.2(h), which is not in the list; adding it would complete the citation.

title: Your Visitation Order
statement: - Holiday or birthday visits, but only if the judge adds them. Ask your lawyer to ask for them.
source_says: (6) Other orders concerning in-person visitation (specify):
steps: Confirmed live with position() (pos 453). Searched 'JV-400 Visitation Attachment', opened the form on courts.ca.gov and read every printed item: supervised or unsupervised, frequency and duration, overnight, location, transportation, other contact, restrictions. There is no printed line for holidays or birthdays; they could only be written into an 'Other (specify)' line by the court. That matches 'only if the judge adds them'.

title: Your Visitation Order
statement: - Tell your social worker and your lawyer what change you want. Ask your lawyer to bring it to the judge.
source_name: Judicial Council booklet Juvenile Dependency Court and You; Cal. Rules of Court rule 5.695(f)(3)
source_says: Before every hearing is a good time for you to talk with your lawyer and the social worker
steps: Confirmed live with position() (pos 588). This is advice, not a legal rule. Opened the booklet: quoted line, plus 'Let your social worker know what you think would be useful to you and your kids' and the 388 example 'You want to ask the court to change your supervised visits to unsupervised visits.' Opened rule 5.695(f)(3): 'the court must order visitation', so a change to the order goes through the judge. Advice fits the sources.

title: Your Visitation Order
statement: - If the judge ordered reunification services for you, the judge must also order visits with your child. No visit order can put your child's safety at risk.
source_name: WIC 362.1(a)(1)(A), (B); Cal. Rules of Court rule 5.695(f)(3)
source_says: for visitation between the parent or guardian and the child. ... No visitation order shall jeopardize the safety of the child.
steps: Confirmed live with position() (pos 860). Searched 'WIC 362.1 visitation as frequent as possible', opened public.law 362.1: (a) lead-in 'any order placing a child in foster care, and ordering reunification services, shall provide as follows', then (a)(1)(A) and (a)(1)(B) (quoted). Opened rule 5.695 on courts.ca.gov, (f)(3): 'If a child is removed ... and reunification services are ordered, the court must order visitation between the child and the parent or guardian for whom services are ordered.' Both sentences match.

title: Your Visitation Order
statement: Welfare & Institutions Code §§ 362.1, 366.21; California Rules of Court, rule 5.695(f)(3); form JV-400
source_name: WIC 362.1; WIC 366.21(h); Cal. Rules of Court rule 5.695(f)(3); form JV-400
source_says: the court must order visitation between the child and the parent or guardian for whom services are ordered.
steps: Confirmed live with position() in legal_reference (pos 1). Opened rule 5.695 on courts.ca.gov and listed its subdivisions: (f) is 'Provision of reunification services' and the visitation text is (f)(3) (quoted, followed by 'Visits are to be as frequent as possible'). Opened public.law 362.1(a)(1)(A), (B) on visits and safety. Opened public.law 366.21: (h) 'unless it finds that visitation would be detrimental to the child'. Opened form JV-400 on courts.ca.gov: 'VISITATION ATTACHMENT: PARENT, LEGAL GUARDIAN, INDIAN CUSTODIAN, OTHER IMPORTANT PERSON', which sets frequency, supervision, location and conditions. All four cites fit the entry.
